analysis.rationale: Compression: block_boundary=4.05/4.86/7.03 (0%FP JPEG), dct_zero_ratio 0.889/0.908/0.924, JPEG severity 4 (jpeg5 raises bb +58%; jpeg4 is closest on all pairs). Blur: gm_ratio 0.123/0.208/0.408, FFT anisotropy 1.24-1.31 (<1.7 -> not motion); glass chosen because raw spectral_slope matches glass5+jpeg4 within 0.03-0.06 on 3/3 pairs (gaussian5 is off 0.22-0.26 on all pairs), gm matches on pairs1/2, wiener kernel corr >0.85 on 3/3. Global: cross-pair target/baseline ratios (glass5+jpeg4) are consistent -> variance x0.718/0.745/0.743, chroma x0.901/0.885/0.853, spread x0.838/na/0.829, mean +5.4/+6.1/+2.4: a linear contrast weaken with effective scale ~0.85. Target unique_G 246/218/236 << JPEG-only sims 255-256 and below contrast-after-JPEG sim (192 at sev1), so the contrast step is applied AFTER JPEG with a milder effective scale than the current library sev1 (c=0.75). Severity 1 is the closest available (var 0.358 vs target 0.456, undershoot 22%; no-contrast overshoots 39%). Noise: no noise step (cross-pair sigma 1.1/0.4; peeled residual structure-dominated, spatial_corr 0.977).
analysis.residual_uncertainty: Global contrast severity is milder in GT (effective c~0.85) than any current severity (sev1=0.75); mean shift (+5.4/+5.8/+2.0) only partially explained by PIL L-pivot (+2.2). Blur subtype glass vs gaussian is a genuine cross-signal conflict (slope/gm -> glass; block_boundary magnitude -> gaussian).
